---
title: "Build an ICRC-1 wallet"
description: "From an ICRC-1 ledger's .did file to a React page that signs in with Internet Identity, shows a balance and sends a transfer that is never paid twice"
---

import { Aside, FileTree } from "@astrojs/starlight/components"

This guide builds a wallet for an ICRC-1 ledger as one small React app. A
person signs in with Internet Identity, sees their balance, and sends a
transfer. It uses the ICP ledger on mainnet. Any ICRC-1 ledger, such as ckBTC,
ckETH or an SNS token, works the same way with its own ledger id.

The app takes care of four things that are easy to get wrong:

- **Amounts** are `bigint` base units. What a person types is read by
  `parseUnits`, which refuses `1,5` or a ninth decimal of ICP instead of
  rounding it.
- **The balance** waits until someone is signed in, and is cached per caller.
- **A lost reply** is never answered by sending a new transfer. The page
  offers the same transfer again, and the ledger answers `Duplicate` if the
  first one went through.
- **A test** runs the transfer against an in-memory replica, with its reply
  lost on purpose, and checks that the ledger is paid once.

When it is done, the project holds these files:

<FileTree>

- icrc1.did the ledger's interface
- src/
  - generated/
    - icrc1.ts written by `candid-core-cli gen`
  - ledger.ts the ledger, its token, and how amounts are shown
  - App.tsx the client and the page
  - SignIn.tsx
  - Balance.tsx
  - transfer.ts a form to a transfer, and the ledger's errors in words
  - Send.tsx
  - transfer.test.ts
  - main.tsx

</FileTree>

## Before you start

Follow steps 0 to 2 of [Getting started](/v4/guides/getting-started/). They
give you:

1. a Vite app made from the `react-ts` template
   ([step 0](/v4/guides/getting-started/#0-create-the-project));
2. the packages, with `@ic-reactor/react` and `@icp-sdk/auth` for the React
   app ([step 1](/v4/guides/getting-started/#1-install));
3. `src/generated/icrc1.ts`, generated from `icrc1.did`
   ([step 2](/v4/guides/getting-started/#2-generate-the-module)).

The test in step 7 also needs Vitest:

```sh
npm install --save-dev vitest
```

<Aside type="caution">
  Signing in and reading cost nothing. A transfer on mainnet moves real ICP
  and pays the ledger's fee. Run the test of [step 7](#7-test-it-without-a-network)
  first. To send on a local network instead, see the
  [Vite wallet](/v4/examples/vite-wallet/) example.
</Aside>

## 1. The ledger and its token

```ts
// src/ledger.ts
import { formatUnits } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import { useClient } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { actor, type Actor } from "./generated/icrc1"

/** The ICP ledger on mainnet. Every ICRC-1 ledger works the same way. */
export const LEDGER_ID = "ryjl3-tyaaa-aaaaa-aaaba-cai"

/** This render's client, and the ledger as its caller calls it. */
export function useLedger() {
  const client = useClient()
  const ledger = client.canister<Actor>(actor, { id: LEDGER_ID })
  return { client, ledger }
}

export interface Token {
  readonly symbol: string
  readonly decimals: number
  /** The transfer fee, in base units. */
  readonly fee: bigint
}

/** The ledger's token, once its three reads have answered. */
export function useToken(): Token | undefined {
  const { client, ledger } = useLedger()
  // A token's symbol and decimals never change: not read again on a remount
  // or a window focus.
  const symbol = useQuery({
    ...client.queryOptions(ledger, "icrc1_symbol"),
    staleTime: Infinity,
  })
  const decimals = useQuery({
    ...client.queryOptions(ledger, "icrc1_decimals"),
    staleTime: Infinity,
  })
  const fee = useQuery(client.queryOptions(ledger, "icrc1_fee"))
  if (
    symbol.data === undefined ||
    decimals.data === undefined ||
    fee.data === undefined
  ) {
    return undefined
  }
  return { symbol: symbol.data, decimals: decimals.data, fee: fee.data }
}

/** An amount in base units, as a person reads it: "1.5 ICP". */
export const showAmount = (units: bigint, token: Token): string =>
  `${formatUnits(units, token.decimals)} ${token.symbol}`
```

- `useLedger()` builds the ledger from the `useClient()` of the render.
  `client.canister()` returns the same object each time, so this costs nothing
  per render. `useClient()` renders its component again when the caller
  changes, so every option built from it uses the current caller's keys.
- The token is three reads. `staleTime: Infinity` keeps symbol and decimals
  from being read again on their own. A transfer still refreshes every read of
  the ledger, these two and the fee included.
- `showAmount` goes through `formatUnits`, never through `Number`, which
  cannot hold every amount a ledger can. See
  [Values and units](/v4/guides/values/#token-amounts).

## 2. The client and the page

```tsx
// src/App.tsx
import { createClient } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import { ReactorProvider } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { AuthClient } from "@icp-sdk/auth/client"
import { Balance } from "./Balance"
import { Send } from "./Send"
import { SignIn } from "./SignIn"

export function App() {
  return (
    <ReactorProvider
      client={() =>
        createClient({
          network: "ic",
          auth: (network) => new AuthClient(network),
        })
      }
    >
      <main>
        <h1>Wallet</h1>
        <SignIn />
        <Balance />
        <Send />
      </main>
    </ReactorProvider>
  )
}
```

The provider calls its `client` factory once and owns the client it makes.
The `auth` factory runs once too, in the browser only, and the client calls
every method as whoever is signed in. Read [Auth](/v4/guides/auth/) for other
sign-ins.

`App` is a named export. Vite's template imports a default one, so make
`src/main.tsx` import it by name:

```tsx
// src/main.tsx
import { StrictMode } from "react"
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client"
import { App } from "./App"

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <App />
  </StrictMode>
)
```

## 3. Sign in

```tsx
// src/SignIn.tsx
import { useAuth } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { useState } from "react"

export function SignIn() {
  const { status, principal, signIn, signOut } = useAuth()
  const [error, setError] = useState<string>()
  // signIn() and signOut() reject when they fail, or when the user closes
  // the Internet Identity window.
  const run = (action: () => Promise<unknown>) => {
    setError(undefined)
    action().catch((reason: unknown) => setError(String(reason)))
  }

  if (status === "signed-in") {
    return (
      <p>
        Signed in as <code>{principal}</code>{" "}
        <button onClick={() => run(signOut)}>Sign out</button>
      </p>
    )
  }
  return (
    <p>
      {status === "expired" && "Your session expired. "}
      <button onClick={() => run(signIn)}>
        Sign in with Internet Identity
      </button>
      {error && <span role="alert"> {error}</span>}
    </p>
  )
}
```

`useAuth()` renders the component again when the status or the principal
changes. Its `status` is `"signed-in"`, `"anonymous"`, `"expired"` or
`"signed-in-elsewhere"`, and only `"signed-in"` can send a transfer.

Internet Identity gives each site its own principal. The principal you get on
`http://localhost:5173` is not the one you get on your deployed site, and ICP
sent to one is not in the other's balance.

## 4. The balance

```tsx
// src/Balance.tsx
import { principal } from "@candid-core/schema"
import { useAuth } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { skipToken, useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { showAmount, useLedger, useToken } from "./ledger"

export function Balance() {
  const { client, ledger } = useLedger()
  const { status, principal: caller } = useAuth()
  const token = useToken()
  const signedIn = status === "signed-in"
  const balance = useQuery(
    client.queryOptions(
      ledger,
      "icrc1_balance_of",
      // Nobody to read for yet: skipToken sends nothing.
      signedIn ? { owner: principal(caller), subaccount: null } : skipToken
    )
  )

  if (!signedIn) return <p>Sign in to see your balance.</p>
  if (balance.isError) return <p role="alert">{balance.error.message}</p>
  if (balance.data === undefined || token === undefined)
    return <p>Balance: …</p>
  return <p>Balance: {showAmount(balance.data, token)}</p>
}
```

- `skipToken` holds the read until there is an account to read. There is no
  placeholder account and no `caller!`.
- `principal(caller)` turns the caller's text into a `Principal`, the branded
  text the generated module takes. The read's key holds the caller, so each
  account's balance is cached apart, and nobody is shown another account's
  balance after a switch, which also removes the last account's reads from
  the cache.
- A transfer refreshes the ledger's reads when it settles, so the balance
  updates without code of its own. See
  [Writes](/v4/guides/writes/#what-a-write-refreshes).

## 5. From a form to a transfer

This file has no React in it. It turns what a person typed into a transfer, or
refuses it before anything is sent, and words each error the ledger can
answer with.

```ts
// src/transfer.ts
import { isPrincipal, principal } from "@candid-core/schema"
import { parseUnits, type Canister, type Client } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import type {
  Account,
  Actor,
  TransferArg,
  TransferError,
} from "./generated/icrc1"
import { showAmount, type Token } from "./ledger"

/** What a person typed in the form. */
export interface TransferForm {
  readonly to: string
  readonly amount: string
}

/** The account and amount the form asks for, or why it is refused. */
export function readForm(
  form: TransferForm,
  token: Token
): { ok: true; to: Account; amount: bigint } | { ok: false; reason: string } {
  const to = form.to.trim()
  if (!isPrincipal(to)) {
    return { ok: false, reason: "The recipient is not a principal." }
  }
  let amount: bigint
  try {
    // Plain decimal text with at most `decimals` fraction digits. "1,5",
    // "1e3" and a ninth decimal of ICP are refused, never rounded.
    amount = parseUnits(form.amount, token.decimals)
  } catch (error) {
    return { ok: false, reason: (error as Error).message }
  }
  if (amount === 0n) return { ok: false, reason: "Send more than zero." }
  return { ok: true, to: { owner: principal(to), subaccount: null }, amount }
}

/**
 * A new transfer argument, with a memo of its own and the IC's time in
 * `created_at_time`. The ledger answers the same argument from the same
 * account `Duplicate` instead of running it twice.
 */
export async function newTransfer(
  client: Client,
  ledger: Canister<Actor>,
  to: Account,
  amount: bigint,
  token: Token
): Promise<TransferArg> {
  return {
    to,
    amount,
    // The fee the page showed: if the ledger's fee has changed since, it
    // answers BadFee rather than charge another one.
    fee: token.fee,
    memo: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16)),
    from_subaccount: null,
    created_at_time: await client.time(ledger),
  }
}

/** What the ledger's Err means, in a sentence. */
export function describeError(err: TransferError, token: Token): string {
  switch (err.tag) {
    case "InsufficientFunds":
      return `Not enough funds: the balance is ${showAmount(err.value.balance, token)}, less than the amount plus the fee.`
    case "BadFee":
      return `The fee is now ${showAmount(err.value.expected_fee, token)}. Send again to pay it.`
    case "Duplicate":
      return `This transfer went through already, in block ${err.value.duplicate_of}. It was not paid twice.`
    case "TooOld":
    case "CreatedInFuture":
      return "The ledger refused the transfer's time. Send it as a new transfer."
    case "TemporarilyUnavailable":
      return "The ledger is unavailable for now. Try again in a moment."
    case "BadBurn":
      return `A burn is at least ${showAmount(err.value.min_burn_amount, token)}.`
    case "GenericError":
      return err.value.message
  }
}
```

- `readForm` checks the recipient with `isPrincipal` and the amount with
  `parseUnits` itself, so the form and the amount sent can never disagree.
- `newTransfer` makes the transfer one the ledger can recognize. With
  `created_at_time` set, the ledger runs an argument from the same account
  once, and answers a repeat `Duplicate`. `client.time(ledger)` reads the IC's
  certified time, which the ledger checks the stamp against, rather than the
  computer's clock. That time moves about once a second, so the memo keeps two
  transfers of the same amount, made in the same second, apart.
- `describeError` has a case for each tag of the generated `TransferError`.
  If a tag were missing, the function could end without returning a string,
  and it would not compile.

## 6. Send

```tsx
// src/Send.tsx
import { useAuth } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { useMutation } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { useState, type FormEvent } from "react"
import { showAmount, useLedger, useToken } from "./ledger"
import { describeError, newTransfer, readForm } from "./transfer"

export function Send() {
  const { client, ledger } = useLedger()
  const { status } = useAuth()
  const token = useToken()
  const [form, setForm] = useState({ to: "", amount: "" })
  const [refusal, setRefusal] = useState<string>()
  // No `retry`: a transfer sent again after a lost reply could pay twice.
  const transfer = useMutation(client.mutationOptions(ledger, "icrc1_transfer"))
  // Offered only after an unknown outcome, and only to the account that sent it.
  const again = client.resendOf(transfer.error, ledger, "icrc1_transfer", {
    dedupedBy: (sent) => sent.created_at_time,
  })

  const onSubmit = async (event: FormEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault()
    if (token === undefined) return
    const read = readForm(form, token)
    if (!read.ok) return setRefusal(read.reason)
    setRefusal(undefined)
    try {
      transfer.mutate(
        await newTransfer(client, ledger, read.to, read.amount, token)
      )
    } catch (error) {
      // client.time() failed: nothing was sent.
      setRefusal(String(error))
    }
  }

  const error = transfer.error
  return (
    <form onSubmit={onSubmit}>
      <p>
        <label>
          To{" "}
          <input
            value={form.to}
            onChange={(e) => setForm({ ...form, to: e.target.value })}
            placeholder="principal"
            spellCheck={false}
          />
        </label>
      </p>
      <p>
        <label>
          Amount{token && ` (${token.symbol})`}{" "}
          <input
            value={form.amount}
            onChange={(e) => setForm({ ...form, amount: e.target.value })}
            inputMode="decimal"
          />
        </label>
      </p>
      {token && (
        <p>Fee: {showAmount(token.fee, token)}, on top of the amount.</p>
      )}
      <button
        disabled={
          status !== "signed-in" || token === undefined || transfer.isPending
        }
      >
        Send
      </button>
      {refusal && <p role="alert">Not sent: {refusal}</p>}
      {transfer.isSuccess && token && (
        <p>
          Sent {showAmount(transfer.variables.amount, token)}, in block{" "}
          {transfer.data.toString()}.
        </p>
      )}
      {error && token && (
        <p role="alert">
          {error.kind === "canister_err"
            ? describeError(error.err, token)
            : error.mayHaveExecuted
              ? "The outcome is unknown: the transfer may have gone through. Check the balance before sending a new one."
              : `Not sent: ${error.message}`}
        </p>
      )}
      {again && (
        <button
          type="button"
          disabled={transfer.isPending}
          onClick={() => transfer.mutate(again.arg)}
        >
          Send the same transfer again
        </button>
      )}
    </form>
  )
}
```

A failed transfer ends one of three ways, and the page says which:

| `transfer.error`                    | What happened                                                          | What the page offers                          |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `kind: "canister_err"`              | the ledger ran the call and refused it; `error.err` is the typed `Err` | the reason, from `describeError`              |
| `mayHaveExecuted: true`             | the reply was lost: the transfer may or may not have gone through      | the balance, read again; the same transfer    |
| any other, `mayHaveExecuted: false` | it was certainly not executed                                          | the message; a new press sends a new transfer |

- The mutation resolves with the `Ok` value, the transfer's block index. An
  `Err` rejects as `canister_err`, so a refused transfer is never shown as
  sent.
- `client.resendOf` offers "Send the same transfer again" only after an
  unknown outcome, only while the account that sent it is signed in, and only
  when `created_at_time` is set, which is what the ledger deduplicates on.
  Pressed, it sends the attempt's own
  argument, memo and time included. If the first one went through, the ledger
  answers `Duplicate`, and the page says so. See
  [Writes](/v4/guides/writes/#sending-the-same-write-again).
- Each press of Send builds a new argument with a new memo, so a new transfer
  is never taken for a repeat of an earlier one.
- There is no `retry` on the mutation, and there must not be one. The client
  re-sends a transfer itself only after a failure that proves the ledger never
  got it. See [Errors and mayHaveExecuted](/v4/guides/errors/).

## 7. Test it without a network

`createTestClient` gives a real client over an in-memory replica. The ledger
is replaced by handlers you write, and a test can lose a reply on purpose:

```ts
// src/transfer.test.ts
import { principal } from "@candid-core/schema"
import { createTestClient } from "@ic-reactor/core/testing"
import { afterEach, beforeEach, expect, it } from "vitest"
import { actor, type Actor } from "./generated/icrc1"
import { LEDGER_ID, type Token } from "./ledger"
import { newTransfer, readForm } from "./transfer"

const token: Token = { symbol: "ICP", decimals: 8, fee: 10_000n }
const to = { owner: principal("aaaaa-aa"), subaccount: null }

let test: ReturnType<typeof createTestClient>
let moved: bigint

beforeEach(() => {
  test = createTestClient() // signed in, as the identity of seed 1
  moved = 0n
  // The ledger's deduplication, in a few lines: the same argument from the
  // same account runs once, and is answered Duplicate after that.
  const blocks = new Map<string, bigint>()
  test.mock<Actor>(actor, LEDGER_ID, {
    icrc1_transfer: (arg, { caller }) => {
      const key = [caller, arg.created_at_time, arg.memo?.join()].join(" ")
      const block = blocks.get(key)
      if (block !== undefined) {
        return {
          tag: "Err",
          value: { tag: "Duplicate", value: { duplicate_of: block } },
        }
      }
      moved += arg.amount
      blocks.set(key, BigInt(blocks.size))
      return { tag: "Ok", value: BigInt(blocks.size - 1) }
    },
  })
})

afterEach(() => test.client.dispose())

it("refuses an amount it cannot send exactly", () => {
  expect(readForm({ to: "aaaaa-aa", amount: "1.5" }, token)).toEqual({
    ok: true,
    to,
    amount: 150_000_000n,
  })
  expect(readForm({ to: "aaaaa-aa", amount: "1,5" }, token).ok).toBe(false)
  expect(readForm({ to: "aaaaa-aa", amount: "0.123456789" }, token).ok).toBe(
    false
  )
  expect(readForm({ to: "alice", amount: "1" }, token).ok).toBe(false)
})

it("pays once when the reply is lost and the same transfer is sent again", async () => {
  const ledger = test.client.canister<Actor>(actor, { id: LEDGER_ID })
  const arg = await newTransfer(test.client, ledger, to, 1n, token)
  test.dropNextReply({ method: "icrc1_transfer" }) // it runs; its reply is lost

  const lost = await ledger.icrc1_transfer(arg).catch((error: unknown) => error)
  expect(lost).toMatchObject({ kind: "outcome_unknown", mayHaveExecuted: true })

  const again = test.client.resendOf(lost, ledger, "icrc1_transfer", {
    dedupedBy: (sent) => sent.created_at_time,
  })
  if (again === undefined) throw new Error("no re-send was offered")
  await expect(again.send()).rejects.toMatchObject({
    kind: "canister_err",
    err: { tag: "Duplicate" },
  })
  expect(moved).toBe(1n) // the ledger ran it once
})
```

```sh
npx vitest run
```

- The handler stands in for the ledger's deduplication. The client, the
  signatures, the certificates and the lost reply are all real.
- `dropNextReply({ method: "icrc1_transfer" })` lets the transfer run and loses
  its reply, so the call rejects with `mayHaveExecuted: true`. The client does
  not send it again by itself.
- `again.send()` sends the identical argument, and the ledger answers
  `Duplicate`. `moved` shows it was paid once.

The test runs in Node, Vitest's default environment. For tests of the
components themselves, see [Testing](/v4/guides/testing/#testing-react).

## 8. Run it

```sh
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:5173` and sign in. The balance reads `0 ICP` for a new
principal. Send ICP to the principal shown, from another wallet, and reload
the page to see it. Then send part of it to another principal: the balance
drops by the amount plus the fee.
